verdicts.summary: Lean uses a different formula here. No multi-index partial-derivative notation ∂^I was found anywhere in the NavierStokes namespace: the Lean measures regularity with the total Fréchet jet ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ j (f n) x‖ and quantifies over the order j ≤ m, not over a five-component multi-index. The chart's five real coordinates do exist (LocalSignedRequest.Point = ℝ × ((ℝ×ℝ) × (ℝ×ℝ)), with the slow pair (Z,T) and harmonic pair (H₁,H₂) read off by BaseContextAssembly.slowCoordinates), so the paper's I ∈ ℕ₀⁵ has a referent, but MemClass itself is stated for an abstract normed space D and never names R, Z, T, H₁, H₂. The two encodings are interchangeable in the direction the paper uses — ‖∂^I a‖ ≤ ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ |I| a‖ for every multi-index I of length |I|, since each coordinate partial is an evaluation of the |I|-linear iterated derivative on unit basis vectors — so the Lean bound is at least as strong as the paper's per-multi-index bound at the same order. I did not find a Lean lemma stating that comparison, and the converse direction (reconstituting the iterated-Fréchet norm from the coordinate partials) costs a dimensional constant; since this display only fixes notation for the bounds (6.24), (6.25) and (6.29), which the Lean states in its own notation, the surrounding results are still proved. Recorded as packaging/notation, not a mathematical gap.
